import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Convert 'has_video_4k' to a more descriptive string for the legend
df['has_video_4k_label'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({1: '4K Video', 0: 'No 4K Video'})

# Set a style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the scatter plot using megapixels vs. price,
# with hue for sensor_type, size for weight, and style for 4K video capability.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',      # Color points by sensor type
    size='weight_grams',    # Size points by weight in grams
    sizes=(100, 800),       # Range for point sizes
    style='has_video_4k_label', # Use different markers for 4K video capability
    markers=['o', 'X'],     # Custom markers: 'o' for No 4K Video, 'X' for 4K Video (assuming default sorting)
    palette='viridis',      # Color palette for hue
    edgecolor='black',      # Add a black edge to markers for better visibility
    linewidth=0.8
)

# Add brand names as labels next to each point for easy identification
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(row['megapixels'] + 0.5, # Offset x-coordinate slightly
             row['price_usd'] + 50,  # Offset y-coordinate slightly
             row['brand'],
             horizontalalignment='left',
             size='small',
             color='black',
             weight='semibold')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type, Weight, and 4K Video', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=13)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=13)

# Get the current legend object and reposition it outside the plot area
legend = plt.gca().legend_
if legend:
    legend.set_bbox_to_anchor((1.05, 1)) # Place legend outside to the right of the plot
    legend.set_loc('upper left')         # Anchor point of the legend itself

# Adjust plot layout to make space for the legend on the right
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.78, 1]) # [left, bottom, right, top] - right=0.78 leaves 22% for legend

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')

# Close the plot to free memory
plt.close()
